evidence: KenshiAgentTelemetry.cpp ProbeMenuOrders: hooks ContextMenuGUI::show and returns early during a probe, then calls ContextMenu::showContextMenu(true, target) and reads ContextMenu::orders before closing it again. Kenshi already separates building the order list from drawing it, so muting the second leaves the first intact and the agent is offered the same list a player sees on right-click, with no widget shown. It refuses to run while a menu is already open and calls through the saved original rather than our own hook, so what the player opened a menu on is never overwritten

The three passive predicates were each measured live and each answers a different question: isOrderValidForSelection returned true for all 291 vocabulary entries; getPlayerTaskProbability is an odds getter that returned exactly KIDNAP_ORDER and STEALTH_KNOCKOUT against a cannibal whose own menu offered ATTACK_ENEMIES and FOCUSED_MELEE_ATTACK; Character::checkPlayerOrderForProblems is not a query at all -- it floated 'I don't have a medkit' over a character, crashed world load twice, and answered 'no problem' for 285 of 291

Both probes still run and the union is reported with provenance, since they disagree in both directions and neither can be subtracted from the other. AdvertisedTask.source records menu or odds, and it travels into the bound reason so an order that binds and then fails to take is attributable without a second live run

KenshiAgentTelemetry.cpp perform_character_order: resolves the wire's lowercased vocabulary name to its TaskType, re-probes with the same ProbeAdvertisedTasks that published the offer so publication and dispatch cannot consult different oracles, adopts an identical active goal via HasExactContextGoal instead of reissuing, then newPlayerTaskSelectedCharacters(task, handle, building, position, false) -- the same generic call that already carries MOVE_CUS_ORDERED and PLAYER_TALK_TO

Target resolution deliberately uses FindExactNearbyCharacter, which applies no disposition filter, rather than FindExactDialogueTarget: an order is not a conversation, and hostiles, the unconscious, and the dead are exactly who orders are for
entries.note: Dispatched live on kae-04-funded-pair: stealth_knockout, unprovoked_focused_melee_attack, attack_enemies, player_talk_to and loot_target each reached goal adoption and finished on context_task_started, none of them a verb written into this repo. Kenshi's own state reasoning arrived with them -- measured live, an unconscious bandit advertised LOOT_TARGET, LIFT_PERSON_PLAYER_ORDER and FIRST_AID_ORDER and no attack, while a conscious one advertised UNPROVOKED_FOCUSED_MELEE_ATTACK and no looting. Both probes earned their place: the knockout that created the lootable body came from the odds getter, and the looting from the menu. The probe budget means an unprobed person reports advertised_tasks_probed false, and both the binding and the affordance treat that as unknown rather than empty. A dispatch whose probe could not run is refused as order_probe_unavailable rather than context_action_unavailable, so 'Kenshi withdrew this order' stays distinct from 'nobody could ask'. Two gaps remain, both past the order rather than in it: roughly a third of orders finish as movement_stalled because the ordered character cannot path to the target, and the order is terminal at goal adoption, so nothing observes the looting that follows -- with the loot window open the agent had no affordance to take anything and waited for a completion no field reports.

evidence: KenshiAgentTelemetry.cpp transfer_item: resolves both owners to handles, requires both inventory windows open, and calls InventoryGUI::RClickAutoTrade(section, x, y, destination, thieveryChecks, first) -- the engine's own right-click transfer, which the five operations it replaces each simulated with a mouse

The verdict is Kenshi's and is reported verbatim rather than collapsed into success or failure: ok, no_room, cant_afford, shopkeeper_cant_afford, cant_wear_item, incompatible_item, locked, thief_detected, selling_stolen_item_detected, thats_mine, target_conscious, smuggling_only, illegal_goods, uniforms, container_not_empty. Inventing a coarser vocabulary on top of a finer one is how selection_mismatch came to mean six conditions

Conservation is measured across the call rather than inferred from the verdict: a permitted transfer that moved nothing terminates as permitted_without_moving rather than as success, because an engine answering OK has said the transfer was allowed, not that an item moved

The slot is the address. RClickAutoTrade takes a section name and an x/y, and UIState.open_inventories exports exactly that per item, so no cell label is scraped from a MyGUI widget and no pointer is used at all
pointer_actions is 0. The operations this subsumes spend 23 pointer actions between them, 12 of those in harvest_resource alone
entries.note: Not yet dispatched live. Requires two inventories open at once, which is why opening one no longer refuses because another already is. Binding proves both inventories open, the section present, and the named item still in its slot, since position alone is not identity.
